Control Vulnerability Description: Refused and denied actions are not audited: a request refused by the role gate (401/403 in auth::layer) or a change refused by a handler (e.g. 409 on update_user) writes no audit row; reads of security objects (accounts, tokens, sign-in settings, configuration export) are not audited.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Write a failure audit row (actor, method, path, address, reason) for every 401/403 and every refused change, and an access row for reads of security objects; both exported as audit.record. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Write a failure audit row (actor, method, path, address, reason) for every 401/403 and every refused change, and an access row for reads of security objects; both exported as audit.record.

Control Vulnerability Description: Sign-ins by client certificate, API token and OpenStare trust are not written to the audit record (no session is created); refused certificates and tokens are only logged.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Audit the first use of each certificate, token and OpenStare identity per connection or per interval, and every refusal. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Audit the first use of each certificate, token and OpenStare identity per connection or per interval, and every refusal.

Control Vulnerability Description: Decision rows (every configuration and track change) carry no client address, and HTTP request details (User-Agent, Referer, X-Forwarded-For) are not recorded.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Record the client address on every decision and add a per-request access event (actor, method, path, status, address, User-Agent). [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Record the client address on every decision and add a per-request access event (actor, method, path, status, address, User-Agent).

Control Vulnerability Description: Any viewer can read account, token and sign-in decisions through GET /api/v1/decisions?op=..., contrary to the admin guide (viewers cannot see accounts).
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Limit /decisions for non-admins to track-management and correlation operations. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Limit /decisions for non-admins to track-management and correlation operations.

Control Vulnerability Description: The source probe (admins) with a file transport reads any file the process can read and is not audited.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Audit every probe (actor, transport, path or address, outcome); restrict file probes to the data directory. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Audit every probe (actor, transport, path or address, outcome); restrict file probes to the data directory.

Control Vulnerability Description: Source changes store the full before/after specification, including inline feed credentials, in the audit table (readable by admins, kept forever).
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Mask secret fields (ot_source::secrets rules) in decision before/after before recording. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Mask secret fields (ot_source::secrets rules) in decision before/after before recording.

Control Vulnerability Description: Error responses reveal internals: 500s return raw SQLite, Redis and file-system error text to any role, and /api/v1/status gives viewers versions, paths, the NATS URL and raw errors.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Return a generic message with a correlation id to non-admins and log the detail; restrict /status details to admins. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Return a generic message with a correlation id to non-admins and log the detail; restrict /status details to admins.

Control Vulnerability Description: The SAML assertion consumer (unauthenticated) parses XML with libxml2 in recovery mode and does not refuse DOCTYPE declarations. External entities are not loaded (no NOENT/DTDLOAD), but recovery mode and DTDs widen the attack surface for XML and signature-wrapping attacks.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Refuse any DOCTYPE in a SAMLResponse before parsing; parse strictly (no recover) with NONET; cap the body size. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Refuse any DOCTYPE in a SAMLResponse before parsing; parse strictly (no recover) with NONET; cap the body size.

Control Vulnerability Description: The session cookie carries Max-Age (the 24 h session lifetime), so it survives closing the browser.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Issue the session cookie without Max-Age/Expires (a browser-session cookie); the server-side session keeps its limits. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Issue the session cookie without Max-Age/Expires (a browser-session cookie); the server-side session keeps its limits.

Control Vulnerability Description: Classification markings are not carried on every output: TAK/CoT events, the CSV track export, the audit CSV, registry sheets and configuration exports carry no marking, and the UI does not show a track's own label.
Milestone with Completion Dates: 0.5.0: Mark each output (CoT detail element, export headers) and show the track label in the UI; or refuse labelled tracks on unmarked outputs. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Mark each output (CoT detail element, export headers) and show the track label in the UI; or refuse labelled tracks on unmarked outputs.

Control Vulnerability Description: The notice-and-consent banner is enforced in the browser only, and admins can reach Settings without accepting it (Go to Settings records acceptance).
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Remove the bypass, record acceptance on the server and refuse API use until it is accepted. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Remove the bypass, record acceptance on the server and refuse API use until it is accepted.

Control Vulnerability Description: Signing out lands on the sign-in page without an explicit sign-out message.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Show 'You have signed out' after a user sign-out. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Show 'You have signed out' after a user sign-out.

Control Vulnerability Description: Accounts cannot be made temporary or emergency with an expiry; break-glass accounts are exempt from the inactivity rule.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Add an optional account expiry (72 h for temporary accounts), disabled by the maintenance sweep and audited. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Add an optional account expiry (72 h for temporary accounts), disabled by the maintenance sweep and audited.

Control Vulnerability Description: A locked account unlocks itself after 15 minutes; the Container Platform SRG asks for the lock to hold until an administrator releases it (the ASD STIG accepts the timed lock).
Milestone with Completion Dates: Product owner decision: Product owner decision: hold the lock until an admin unlocks it, or accept the risk citing the ASD STIG. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Product owner decision: hold the lock until an admin unlocks it, or accept the risk citing the ASD STIG.

Control Vulnerability Description: New passwords are not checked against a list of commonly used or compromised passwords.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Check password::check against a shipped blocklist (updatable, e.g. from NIST SP 800-63B sources). [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Check password::check against a shipped blocklist (updatable, e.g. from NIST SP 800-63B sources).

Control Vulnerability Description: Listening sources can accept unauthenticated devices: UDP and multicast, TCP server without client_ca_file, gRPC server without a bearer token.
Milestone with Completion Dates: 0.5.0: Require mTLS or a token on listening sources unless explicitly allowed, and list the exception in the hardening checklist. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Require mTLS or a token on listening sources unless explicitly allowed, and list the exception in the hardening checklist.

Control Vulnerability Description: Release images are signed with cosign's standard (non-FIPS) cryptography and a file key.
Milestone with Completion Dates: 0.5.0: Sign with a FIPS-validated module (Go FIPS mode or a KMS/HSM key). [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Sign with a FIPS-validated module (Go FIPS mode or a KMS/HSM key).

Control Vulnerability Description: The user interface and the administration functions share one listener and sign-in; only role checks separate them.
Milestone with Completion Dates: 0.5.0: Add an optional admin-only listener (e.g. OT_ADMIN_BIND) so a site can put administration on a management network. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Add an optional admin-only listener (e.g. OT_ADMIN_BIND) so a site can put administration on a management network.

Control Vulnerability Description: Multicast (UDP sources and TAK SA output) is IPv4 only.
Milestone with Completion Dates: 0.5.0: Add IPv6 multicast and IPv6 tests. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Add IPv6 multicast and IPv6 tests.

Control Vulnerability Description: Development process documents are missing: configuration management plan, threat model, coding standards, security incident response and disclosure process (SECURITY.md), security advisories, code coverage.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Write docs/security/{scm-plan,threat-model,coding-standards}.md and SECURITY.md; publish GitHub Security Advisories; add coverage to CI. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Write docs/security/{scm-plan,threat-model,coding-standards}.md and SECURITY.md; publish GitHub Security Advisories; add coverage to CI.

Control Vulnerability Description: The sample docker-compose.yml uses host networking, a bind mount, and no CPU, memory or process limits.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Ship a bridge network with only 8090 published, a named volume and resource limits; document host networking as an exception. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Ship a bridge network with only 8090 published, a named volume and resource limits; document host networking as an exception.

Control Vulnerability Description: The v0.4.2 image has 5 Critical, 61 High, 99 Medium and 90 Low findings, all in Debian 12 base packages (perl-base, util-linux, libxml2, zlib, ncurses, ...), none with a fix at scan time (tzdata has one).
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Rebuild on the current base; move to a minimal runtime image carrying only what the binary, SAML (libxml2/xmlsec) and the OpenSSL FIPS provider need. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Rebuild on the current base; move to a minimal runtime image carrying only what the binary, SAML (libxml2/xmlsec) and the OpenSSL FIPS provider need.

Control Vulnerability Description: Dependency advisories and the image scan run only on push or release, not on a schedule.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Scheduled workflow (daily) running cargo deny, npm audit and scripts/ato/scan on the latest release. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Scheduled workflow (daily) running cargo deny, npm audit and scripts/ato/scan on the latest release.

Control Vulnerability Description: The ports, protocols and services are not listed in one place for PPSM registration.
Milestone with Completion Dates: Next 0.4 release: Add a PPSM table (port, protocol, direction, purpose, default) to the admin guide. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Add a PPSM table (port, protocol, direction, purpose, default) to the admin guide.

Control Vulnerability Description: The Content Security Policy allows inline styles (style-src 'unsafe-inline'), which React, MapLibre and CodeMirror need (finding F-5).
Milestone with Completion Dates: 0.5.0: Move inline styles to classes or nonces where the libraries allow; accept the residual risk otherwise. [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Move inline styles to classes or nonces where the libraries allow; accept the residual risk otherwise.

Control Vulnerability Description: Client-certificate revocation is checked with CRLs only (end-entity), not OCSP.
Milestone with Completion Dates: 0.5.0: OCSP with stapling or responder queries (#21). [[DATE]]
Recommendations: OCSP with stapling or responder queries (#21).

Control Vulnerability Description: No formal criticality analysis of components (SA-15(3)); security-critical parts are identified only in fips.md and the fork notes.
Milestone with Completion Dates: 0.5.0: Add a criticality analysis to the threat model (P-20). [[DATE]]
Recommendations: Add a criticality analysis to the threat model (P-20).
